st.t: Photo Gallery - 1971, Mandir Murti-pratishtha Mahotsav, Sankari, India
w: Sankari is a very small village with a population of no more than a hundred people and a single street of homes. Lush farms and trees surround the village. Pramukh Swami Maharaj consecrated the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Laxminarayan Dev in Sankari on 3 June, 1971. It was Swamishri's first murti-pratishtha of a shikharbaddh mandir.

Accompanied by Pujya Sant Swami and Pujya Mahant Swami, Swamishri graced the Nagar Yatra prior to the murti pratishtha ceremony. The murti pratishtha ceremony was performed with due vedic chants and rituals. At the conclusion of the pratishtha, Swamishri held up a miror to the Murti so that the first thing that the Lord saw through the murti's eyes was His own murti. It is not very common that the mirror, due to the force of the light emerging from the murti, cracks. But this miracle happened in Sankari, marking an auspicious and glorious beginning for Swamishri's consecration of more than 350 Mandirs. And true to this miracle, every Annakut festival, the Sankari Thakorji confirms His presence by accepting one of the food items offered to Him. At this occassion of Murti-pratishtha a devotee called Natvarbhai created and sang the famous bhajan " Vhala Akshardhamana Vaasi Maare Haiye Karjo Vaas "

The number of Mandirs being consecrated by Swamishri is still growing, with his conviction that what the world today needs is centers of morality, ethics and spirituality - Mandirs help humanity orient itself towards better living and aim towards the divine.

Devotees joined with enthusiasm in bullock carts, cars, and on foot in the Nagar Yatra Women carrying kalashas during the Nagar Yatra The priest conducting the pratishtha ceremony performs pujan of Swamishri. To his right is P. Sant Swami and P. Mahant Swami
The volunteers (karyakars), endeavoring for the Satsang activities in Mumbai, performed various programs in the presence of Swamishri.

In the evening, the volunteers (karyakars) performed small skits on the problems they face while doing Satsang activities before Swamishri and an audience of devotees. In his blessings, Swamishri stressed, "; It is true that our financial position and earnings are a source of worries. But one should not spend more than one’s income. We should balance our spendings. Sometimes when we are faced with unexpected expenditures, we should be patient, strong and endeavor to earn more. Since the cost of living is very high, the family should cut down on entertainment costs or other luxurious spendings. The children too should reduce their unnecessary academic expenditures. If all the members of the family try to understand then the financial situation will not cause anxiety and misery in your daily work..." Swamishri also talked about punctuality, sincerity in Satsang activities and teamwork.

In the evening assembly, Swamishri emphasized the importance of attending the Sunday assembly: "The 'Sunday Assembly' was introduced by Yogiji Maharaj. It was his wish that everyone should come together and attend the 'Sunday Assembly.' Initially he used to write postcards to devotees regarding the assembly program of dhun, prayer and reading of Vachnamrut and Swamini Vato. Then as the numbers increased the weekly agenda was printed in the 'Patrika.' He had also instructed that every devotee should have a home-mandir in which arti and thal be performed. He insisted upon this so that in doing our mundane activities we do not forget God.

"It was Yogiji Maharaj's instruction that one should forfeit the profit of Rs.25,000 and attend the Sunday Assembly. Through samagam one attains spiritual strength which solves many of our problems ..."

At 10.15 a.m., Swamishri arrived to perform the yagna rituals of the murtis of Ghanshyam Maharaj (Surendranagar) and murtis to be consecrated in the hari mandirs of Halvad, Kharwa and Rangpur. Swamishri performed pujan and arti of the murtis. In his blessing Swamishri said, "The satsang in Jhalavad region is strong. The devotees perform puja daily and visit daily for darshan in the mandirs. Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj have visited Limbdi and neighboring villages on many occasions..."
From 6.00 p.m.
During the meetings, a youth asked Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "How can celibacy be kept in married life?"

Swamishri said, "For a householder, 'one wife, always a brahmachari'. Faithfulness to one wife. He should not let his mind go elsewhere. Relations with his wife, but any other woman he should regard as a mother or sister. And we sadhus have to keep celibacy in all eight ways."
The youth asked, "If we do not marry and want to keep celibacy, is it necessary to wear these sadhu's clothes?"
Swamishri said, "No, nothing like that. Many have lived in that way. But in these clothes, one only has to take care not to slip somewhere."

In Edison, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj goes from his residence to the assembly venue, different police officers come respectfully every day to escort his car on the way. Mostly they are American police. Today a young Gujarati had come on duty as a policeman. Swamishri asked his name. He said, "Milan Patel."
"And your village?"
"Bhadran."
While talking with Swamishri, he was speaking partly in English and partly in Gujarati. Swamishri said to him, "We must not forget Gujarati."
"Why?" he asked in return.
Laughing, Swamishri said, "So that you are able to talk with someone like me!"
Milan said, "Yes, yes."

Milan could understand everything, but he had to think a lot to express himself. Swamishri said to him, "Look, we have to take care that our language does not disappear. If our language is preserved, our culture and our dharma will also be preserved. And so we should keep the Gujarati language going in daily life."

Milan agreed about this. Swamishri has inspired countless youths like Milan to keep their mother tongue alive. Milan felt that he was only a protector of the law, whereas Swamishri is the protector and nurturer of a vast culture.

The evening celebration of Yogiji Jayanti was based on the theme of the kirtan, Ek kathE3 tame sau sE3mbhaljo. The assembly was interspersed with dance, drama and speeches. After the opening traditional dance by children Brahmadarshan Swami talked about the spiritual bonds between Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Ghanshyamcharan Swami discoursed about the vicharan of Yogiji Maharaj. This was followed by a drama performed by children and youths depicting the harmful effects of addiction. Another drama by youths from ‘Yogi Smaran Yatra’ showed the impression Yogiji Maharaj had on Colonel Bhatia. Viveksagar Swami talked about Pramukh Swami Maharaj as the successor of Yogiji Maharaj. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “God is the doer of whatever that happens in the world, because He pervades in all things. Because he resides everywhere we are able to experience joy. If one believes that there is no God then one will cease to exist because God resides in one’s heart. Yogiji Maharaj was a simple sadhu. He saw the good in all and never saw their faults. He had the vision to see God in all. He respected everyone85” More than 12,000 devotees performed arti in conclusion to the parayan.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti for seven BAPS kutir and hari mandirs: Amba Talat – Nayakpada, Tejlav – Vad Faliya, Chasmandva, Saraiya – Kundal Faliya, Torvan – Donja, Khudvel, and Talavchora – Baroliya. The tribals living in these villages were transformed through the efforts of Swamishri and sadhus. Their wayward lives due to addictions and stealing took a drastic turn because of satsang.
Today, during the meetings, a South Indian spiritual seeker named Murugan folded both hands and said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "I want to become free from the three gunas (qualities)."
Hearing this request, joy spread over Swamishri's face. Swamishri said to this seeker, "You have spoken of becoming gunatit (beyond the qualities). You have asked for something very good."
It was natural that Swamishri should be pleased with a seeker with such spiritual thirst, because this is his main work.

A youth came for darshan. He had complained to Pramukh Swami Maharaj in a letter: "For a long time I have been longing for your personal darshan, but at your place important people are allowed to meet you without reason, and small people like us are left out."
Swamishri said to him, "There is nothing like that with us. You have just come from outside, so go and see what sort of people are sitting there."

Having said this, Swamishri said nothing more, but later, when that youth met a sadhu, he said, "All my illusions were shattered. I noticed outside that only devotees from villages, who looked completely ordinary, were sitting there."
During the walk, Punyakirti Swami phoned from Sarangpur. The 167 students studying in Standard 10 in Sarangpur had all passed. The result was 100%. He gave this news.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj took the phone in his hand and, speaking to him and the teachers sitting around him, said, "Congratulations to the teachers. Congratulations to you too. The school has a good result. My blessings that it always comes like this....."

Swamishri was still speaking when Punyakirti Swami tried to say something in between, so Swamishri stopped him and said, "You should not speak in between like this. When you were speaking, did I speak in between?" Saying this, he burst out laughing and then continued his blessings: "Everyone has worked hard. The teachers have also worked hard. The teachers are good. The boys too have worked hard and are working hard. Moreover, the best thing is that you do it without tuition. So you can be called first in the Board. My blessings that you, the teachers and the students all receive strength."
